info.description:
Read the indexes available in your tenant and the customer profiles within them. To build the queries and indexes this API serves, and to configure it in Amperity, see [Database Profile API](https://docs.amperity.com/operator/api_profile.html).

Every request must include an access token. To create an API key, generate an access token, and find your tenant ID, see [How to authenticate with Amperity APIs](https://docs.amperity.com/api/authentication.html).

**Rate limit.** The Database Profile API accepts up to 2,000 requests per second across your tenant, including its sandboxes. Requests over the limit may return HTTP 429. To ask for a higher limit, contact Amperity Support or your Customer Success Manager.

**Response times.** p95 response times are under 100 ms at 1,000 requests per second. They vary with the size of an index; see **List profiles in an index** for measurements.

get.description:
Return the profiles in an index that match the filter criteria.

### Filter fields

Filter the profiles on any of the index's filter fields by adding a `filter[<field>]=<value>` query parameter for each one. Filter fields are defined by the query that builds the index, and each filter field has the same name as its field in that query. Use filter fields for lookups that match many profiles, such as all of the profiles associated with a reservation ID.

For example, to return the profiles for Daniel Kulhman:

```
GET /indexes/{index-id}/profiles?filter[first_name]=Daniel&filter[last_name]=Kulhman
```

### Response times

The Database Profile API returns p95 response times under 100 ms at 1,000 requests per second. Response times vary with the number of rows, columns, and filter fields in an index: as an index grows and gains filter fields, its requests slow down and it takes longer to build. Indexes with 5 or more filter fields are noticeably slower. An index may have at most 30 fields.

The following measurements were taken with traffic across many endpoints at once, from US East to US West. Use them as a guide to the response times your tenant will see. Each p95 was measured at 1,000 requests per second unless another rate is shown.

| Columns | Filter fields | p95 at 1M rows | p95 at 10M rows | p95 at 100M rows | Build time (1M / 10M / 100M rows) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0 | 74 ms | 48 ms | 84 ms | 2 m 43 s / 3 m 40 s / 26 m |
| 5 | 1 | 140 ms | 150 ms | 240 ms | 2 m 25 s / 3 m 19 s / 29 m |
| 5 | 3 | 3,500 ms at 330/s | 19,000 ms at 40/s | 44,000 ms at 4/s | 3 m 2 s / 4 m 59 s / 34 m |
| 10 | 0 | 48 ms | 52 ms | 100 ms | 2 m 25 s / 3 m 40 s / 42 m |
| 10 | 1 | 150 ms | 200 ms | 290 ms | 2 m 29 s / 3 m 50 s / 43 m |
| 10 | 3 | 1,400 ms at 300/s | 15,000 ms at 50/s | 40,000 ms at 5/s | 3 m 14 s / 5 m / 50 m |
| 10 | 5 | 1,500 ms at 300/s | 11,000 ms at 40/s | 50,000 ms at 5/s | 2 m 32 s / 4 m 10 s / 49 m |
| 30 | 0 | 89 ms | 91 ms | 120 ms | 2 m 50 s / 7 m 14 s / 2 h |
| 30 | 1 | 150 ms | 3,700 ms at 700/s | not measured | 2 m 32 s / 5 m 39 s / not measured |
| 30 | 3 | 1,400 ms at 300/s | 11,000 ms at 40/s | not measured | 3 m 14 s / 6 m 51 s / not measured |
| 30 | 5 | 1,500 ms at 300/s | 8,700 ms at 40/s | not measured | 2 m 32 s / 6 m 38 s / not measured |
| 30 | 10 | 3,800 ms at 150/s | 22,000 ms at 20/s | not measured | 2 m 42 s / 6 m 54 s / not measured |
